newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn stable, watch U.S. soymeal prices.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn stable, watch U.S. soymeal prices.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices were stable on Tuesday as players waited further declines in the U.S. soymeal market following a price plunge overnight, traders said.
"Some importers will take the opportunity to cover some soymeal but not all," one trader said. "This is because prices are expected to come down further in the long term."
"Prices have been so high for so long because of low nearby stocks. My long-term feeling is that prices will come down."
He said buyers seeking to take advantage of the price fall in the United States would be looking at forward positions where declines were the most severe.

October, December, January and March soymeal futures fell the $10.00 per ton daily limit on Monday, pummelled by news that the U.S. Department of Agriculture pegged 1997 soybean acreage at the highest level in 15 years.
Nearby July was down $4.20 at $258.00 a ton.
The USDA's projection for 70.85 million acres of soybeans was above average trade expections of 68.4 million acres.
Another Indonesian trader said soymeal supply in the local market remained ample, adding that feedmills and traders were unlikely to buy from the United States at the moment.
"I think players will generally want to wait and see how the price develops," he said. "Supply is ample (in Indonesia) at the moment, and the feeling is U.S. prices might fall further."
He said Indian soymeal was quoted at $332-$335 a tonne C&F and South America origin at $280 C&F.
Soymeal was quoted at 885-890 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, compared with 900 rupiah a week ago. Corn was quoted unchanged at 380 rupiah/kg.
The traders said the corn market was relatively quiet, with imports continuing to arrive.
They said the corn harvest in the key growing region of Lampung in south Sumatra was tapering off, while the harvest in East Java had begun although supply was just trickling in.
"The East Java harvest will peak towards October," one trader said. "We are getting very small amounts presently."
He said Chinese corn was being at $137/tonne, while Panamax-sized U.S. shipments were quoted at $133-$135 C&F.
